title: Appelles the Painter, or What Do You Do if You Cannot Predict?
hook: Refundable chairs can be wiser than a perfect forecast of the crowd.
counterintuition: Weak prediction asks for design. Cap the loss, keep the option, and let favorable surprise matter without pretending the future is clear.
tryThisNow: Take one plan and cap its worst loss before you try to improve its forecast.
keyTakeaway: Design the position so being wrong stays survivable and being lucky can still matter.

implementationPlan.title: Design The Position So Being
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Train yourself to cap ruin, keep options open, and prefer asymmetry under opacity. Practice it by naming what the visible evidence can and cannot prove.

ifThenPlans.plan: If the project sounds too smooth, then ask how it survives being wrong.
If you cannot predict the path cleanly, then preserve moves that keep learning possible.
If your plan relies on a delicate story, then rebuild it for survivability first.
If a choice starts leaning on Appelles the Painter, then write the missing pressure beside it before approving the next step.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Audit one exposure in your life or work and identify where ruin is still too cheap.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Keep a short log of decisions and whether their downside is capped and their upside stays open.
